note: The closing-reference rule tools/land.sh applies before it merges (#566, #578) and .claude/workflows/review-queue.js applies before it reviews (#688), as one table both test companions run (#745): tools/land_tests.py runs land.sh against each row, and review-queue_tests.mjs runs the script's own rule against each, so a change to either copy that the other does not make turns one of them red. A row is a description, the messages of the non-merge commits between the base and the head, oldest first, and what the rule answers: unnamed, every ticket a closing reference names that no commit names, in the description's order and once for each time it is written ([] when the description merges), or otherRepository, the owner/repo#n form the description is refused for. A merge's message never counts; each companion shows that in its own terms, since land.sh reads git's parents and the script reads a parent count. The rule reads bytes as ASCII: land.sh reads it in the C locale whatever its caller's, and a row marked locales: true is run by tools/land_tests.py under C.UTF-8 as well as C, so a land.sh that read its caller's classes would answer it otherwise.
